doc.title: Arthur Davis and Andy Mosley Interview, 1960-01-12

title: Work songs while working: quartet, cement, and field gangs
summary: One man describes singing in a spiritual quartet, and they explain what work songs accompany: cement, cutting wood, chopping cotton and corn, and singing to ease labor.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Yes, I used to sing in the quartet spiritually. The name of the quartet was the Hummer King. And what are y'all doing while you sing this song? We are peeing in the sidewalks and like when they cement and stuff like that, you know, picking up the waste and wet cement. What do you use? We use showers and pigs in a hard place when they're stuck and you can't get them out. Oh yeah, that's it.
Oh, what I get my new heart filled. Oh, baby, I feel my tender up high. Oh, baby, I feel my tender up high.

Oh, baby, I feel my tender up high. One of those songs is probably like that is, they're probably the great multivine work here. Oh yeah, see, they work like they're be cutting wood in the woods. They're probably be cutting chains, pouring cotton, pouring corn, and different other kind of things. It's early in the morning when they're ringing up their plows and things going to work. But mostly occasionally that's mostly a lot of satisfaction to the guys, and to be singing like that. When they be singing mostly all the time, they say they're singing in the squad, like they're behind flat weed and saying, probably a load in a buggy or something. You're from the country? No, sir, from New Orleans. You didn't do this type of work before then, huh? No, sir. So you learned that up here? Yes, sir. Singing and all that? Yes, sir. From different guys, they be singing and we all work together. I guess you could play the dozens in New Orleans, huh? You know about that. Who's that? Me, that's myself, Gitar and Matthew Maxey. Now what are you doing on this song? I'm just picking. I'm thinking some parts that I'm humming along with Keeping Up The Background. No, but I mean what kind of work would you do with this song? It was Horn King. Most of those songs like that, when he starts singing, will give you the spirit to work with, and the man, your boss man, you can tell him too. And have him out enjoying the work as well as you're doing it.
